title: Point-fibre transport of the smooth trace-cup pairing
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, integers $r,n\geq1$, $q=p^r$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and its algebraic closure $k$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, separated of finite type, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $a:X\to s$ be the structure morphism, with the exceptional admissibility and operations of [def-pod-conventions]. Use completed operations integrally, their scalar localization over $E$, and their common finite coefficient-stage versions over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$ [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x].

Put
$$C=Ra_!K,\quad\omega=Ra^!\Lambda_s,\quad L=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega),\quad D=Ra_*L,\quad H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s).$$
Here tensor and internal Hom are the operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Write $\varepsilon_L:La^*D\to L$ and $\mu:Ra_!\omega\to\Lambda_s$ for the ordinary and exceptional counits [fix-prop-adjunctions], and $P_T=\operatorname{PF}_{a,K,T}:C\otimes^LT\to Ra_!(K\otimes^LLa^*T)$ for the projection transformation [def-exchange-projection].
Define $e=\operatorname{ev}_{K,\omega}\circ(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)$, $p_s=\mu\circ Ra_!e\circ P_D$, and $b_s=\operatorname{curry}(p_s):D\to H$, where evaluation $\operatorname{ev}$ and $\operatorname{curry}$ are those of the restricted tensor--internal-Hom adjunction [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions] (2), as in [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. Use $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], its coherent tensor and unit comparisons [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]
$$\tau_{M,N}:F(M\otimes^LN)\xrightarrow{\sim}FM\otimes^L_\Lambda FN,\qquad u_0:F\Lambda_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda,$$
and put $c=FC$, $c^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)$, $p=u_0\circ Fp_s\circ\tau_{C,D}^{-1}$. Let $\kappa:FH\to c^\vee$ be the coefficient tensor--Hom transpose of $u_0\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s})\circ\tau_{C,H}^{-1}$. For the canonical identity-adjunction isomorphism $u:\omega_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$ and point-dualizing comparison $j:F(R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_s))\xrightarrow{\sim}c^\vee$ of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], put $\rho=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,u)$. Then $j=\kappa\circ F\rho$, $\kappa$ is an isomorphism, and
$$\operatorname{ev}^{\mathrm{coeff}}\circ(1_c\otimes\kappa)=u_0\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s})\circ\tau_{C,H}^{-1}.$$
For every $V\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ and $v:V\to H$, the coefficient transpose of $u_0\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s}\circ(1_C\otimes v))\circ\tau_{C,V}^{-1}$ is $\kappa\circ Fv$.

Let $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ with its evaluation [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x], let $\eta_X:\omega\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ be the canonical smooth orientation of [def-pod-conventions], and let
$$\theta:FD\xrightarrow{\sim}Q=R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$$
be the comparison induced by the evaluation-compatible isomorphism $L\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee(d)[2d]$ of [thm-sf-dual-perfect]. For the actual mixed-support cup product of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product] and the normalized trace of [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing], the resulting Poincare pairing $\beta_K:c\otimes^LQ\to\Lambda$ and its tensor--Hom transpose satisfy
$$\beta_K=p\circ(1_c\otimes\theta^{-1}),\qquad b_K^\sharp=\kappa\circ Fb_s\circ\theta^{-1}.$$
These are identities of derived morphisms at the fixed coefficient stage; the trace uses the same orientation $\eta_X$ as $\theta$.

source.place: first paragraph: smooth dual identification and pairing as evaluation/counit; third paragraph: the specified pairing induces the adjoint; evaluation-preserving point transport at all four stages

proof.text: All the displayed maps have the required finite-Tor domains. Apply [thm-sf-ctf-stability] to $a$, to the coefficient unit, and to $K$: $\omega=Ra^!\Lambda_s$ and $L=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega)$ are finite-Tor constructible, as are $C=Ra_!K$, $D=Ra_*L$ and $H=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s)$. Pullback and tensor preserve these domains as well. At $\mathcal O_E$, [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] and [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] give that $D$ and $C$ lie in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)=D^b_{ctf}$, and clause (vii) gives the integral internal Hom and exceptional adjoint, the finite reductions, and the passage to $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$; the hypotheses on $a$ are precisely the separated finite-type hypotheses in the item. The restricted tensor--Hom adjunction of [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions] (2) therefore applies to $C$ and to $K$. In particular all evaluations and transposes below are on these domains.

source.place: first paragraph: domains of the operations in the pairing

proof.text: For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and $\mathcal O_E$, apply [lem-pod-point-integral-evaluation-normalization] with this $C$: its $H,c,\kappa,\rho,j$ are exactly ours, with the specified tensor and unit comparisons. It gives that $\kappa$ is an isomorphism and $j=\kappa\circ F\rho$, including completed evaluation integrally. For $\Lambda=E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [lem-pod-point-field-evaluation-normalization] gives these same two conclusions for the specified localized and common-stage maps. Thus this step uses normalization of actual maps, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between their source and target. The identity-adjunction normalization of $u$ in both cited statements is the one fixed in the item.

source.place: third paragraph: evaluation-preserving point-category identifications at all four stages

proof.text:
Write $E_C=u_0\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s})\circ\tau_{C,H}^{-1}$. By the definition $\kappa=\operatorname{curry}(E_C)$, the inverse-adjunction identity of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] gives $\operatorname{ev}^{\mathrm{coeff}}\circ(1_c\otimes\kappa)=E_C$. For any $v:V\to H$, naturality of $\tau$ in [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] gives
$$u_0\circ F(\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s}\circ(1_C\otimes v))\circ\tau_{C,V}^{-1}=E_C\circ(1_c\otimes Fv).$$
The uncurrying/precomposition identity in [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] identifies the right side with the uncurrying of $\kappa\circ Fv$. Since uncurrying is a bijection, its transpose is precisely $\kappa\circ Fv$. This proves both the evaluation equation and the universal assertion for $V,v$.

source.place: third paragraph: the specified pairing induces the adjoint, evaluated at the point

proof.text:
Put $N=K^\vee(d)[2d]$ and write $h:L\xrightarrow{\sim}N$ for [thm-sf-dual-perfect]. Its evaluation compatibility says, with $\operatorname{ev}^{\mathrm{tw}}:K\otimes^LN\to\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ the twisted shifted coefficient evaluation,
$$\operatorname{ev}^{\mathrm{tw}}\circ(1_K\otimes h)=\eta_X\circ\operatorname{ev}_{K,\omega}.$$
Here the coefficient evaluation is exactly that of [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x]; $K$ is site-perfect, as required by [thm-sf-dual-perfect]. Thus the twist, shift, and orientation in this equation are the same ones used to define $\theta$. No new orientation is chosen. The shift $[2d]$ is retained with its canonical tensor/shift comparisons in the notation $N$.

source.place: first paragraph: smooth dual identification compatible with evaluation

proof.text:
Write $D_N=Ra_*N$, $t=Ra_*h$, and
$$M_L=Ra_!(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)\circ P_D,\qquad M_N=Ra_!(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_N)\circ P_{D_N}.$$
The ordinary counit of [fix-prop-adjunctions] is natural, so $\varepsilon_N\circ La^*t=h\circ\varepsilon_L$. The projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection] is natural in its second argument, so
$$P_{D_N}\circ(1_C\otimes t)=Ra_!(1_K\otimes La^*t)\circ P_D.$$
Substitution and functoriality give the full needed cup square:
$$M_N\circ(1_C\otimes t)=Ra_!(1_K\otimes h)\circ M_L.$$
By [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product], $FM_L\circ\tau_{C,D}^{-1}$ and $FM_N\circ\tau_{C,D_N}^{-1}$ are exactly the mixed-support products, with the point identifications understood. This calculation also applies with the twist and shift in $N$; the shifted product in the pairing definition is this product read through its canonical shift comparisons.

source.place: first and third paragraphs: the actual mixed-support cup product is projection followed by the ordinary counit

proof.text:
Before applying $F$, the trace-cup pairing with second input $D_N$ is
$$B_N=\mu\circ Ra_!(\eta_X^{-1})\circ Ra_!(\operatorname{ev}^{\mathrm{tw}})\circ M_N.$$
This is exactly [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing]: the normalized trace is the exceptional counit through $\eta_X$, and the preceding arrow is twisted shifted coefficient evaluation. Using the cup square of step 5 and the evaluation equation of step 4, cancel $\eta_X^{-1}\eta_X$ to obtain
$$B_N\circ(1_C\otimes t)=\mu\circ Ra_!(\operatorname{ev}_{K,\omega})\circ M_L=p_s.$$
Apply $F$, compose with $u_0$, and use naturality of $\tau$ from [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Under the canonical direct-image/shift identification $F D_N=Q$, $Ft$ is the stipulated $\theta$. Hence $\beta_K\circ(1_c\otimes\theta)=p$, or equivalently $\beta_K=p\circ(1_c\otimes\theta^{-1})$. This is equality of the specified derived morphisms, with the same $\eta_X$ in the two occurrences.

source.place: first paragraph: cup product, evaluation and normalized trace; third paragraph: the actual pairing

proof.text:
Since $b_s=\operatorname{curry}(p_s)$, [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] gives $p_s=\operatorname{ev}_{C,\Lambda_s}\circ(1_C\otimes b_s)$. Apply step 3 with $V=D$ and $v=b_s$: the transpose of $p$ is $\kappa\circ Fb_s$. Precomposition in the second tensor factor by $\theta^{-1}$ corresponds to precomposition of its transpose, by the same uncurrying/precomposition law. Step 6 therefore gives
$$b_K^\sharp=\operatorname{curry}(\beta_K)=\kappa\circ Fb_s\circ\theta^{-1}.$$
Every equality used only the operations at the chosen coefficient stage, so this also proves the stated fixed-stage interpretation.

source.place: third paragraph: its tensor--Hom transpose is the specified adjoint

proof_origin.place: first and third paragraphs, with explicit evaluation and cup-naturality equations
